The **2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election** took place on **3 May 2012**, alongside other local elections across England. Stockport Council is a unitary authority in Greater Manchester, and in 2012, it was under **no overall control (NOC)**, meaning no single party held a majority of seats.

Here’s a detailed breakdown of the election:

---

### **Key Details**
- **Election Date:** 3 May 2012
- **Council Composition (Pre-Election):**
  - **Liberal Democrats:** 28 seats
  - **Labour:** 21 seats
  - **Conservatives:** 10 seats
  - **People Matter (Independent Group):** 1 seat
  - **Total Seats:** 60 (30 needed for a majority)
- **Turnout:** ~35% (varies by ward)
- **Wards Contested:** 21 of 21 (all seats up for election in thirds, with some wards electing multiple councillors)

---

### **Results Summary**
The election saw **no major shift in control**, but the **Liberal Democrats lost seats**, while **Labour made gains**. The Conservatives remained stable, and an independent candidate won a seat.

#### **Post-Election Composition (2012-2014):**
| Party               | Seats Won (2012) | Change | Total Seats (Post-Election) |
|---------------------|------------------|--------|-----------------------------|
| **Liberal Democrats** | 8                | -4     | **24**                      |
| **Labour**           | 11               | +4     | **25**                      |
| **Conservatives**    | 2                | 0      | **10**                      |
| **People Matter**    | 0                | -1     | **0**                       |
| **Independent**      | 1                | +1     | **1**                       |
| **Total**            | **22**           |        | **60**                      |

*(Note: Only 21 seats were up for election in 2012, as Stockport elects by thirds. The "Total Seats" column reflects the full council composition after the election.)*

---

### **Notable Outcomes**
1. **Liberal Democrat Losses**
   - The Lib Dems lost **4 seats**, reducing their total from **28 to 24**.
   - They lost ground in **Brinnington & Central** (to Labour) and **Edgeley & Cheadle Heath** (also to Labour).
   - Their leader, **Dave Goddard**, held his seat in **Stepping Hill** but with a reduced majority.

2. **Labour Gains**
   - Labour gained **4 seats**, increasing their total from **21 to 25**.
   - Key wins included:
     - **Brinnington & Central** (from Lib Dem)
     - **Edgeley & Cheadle Heath** (from Lib Dem)
     - **Reddish North** (from Lib Dem)
   - Labour became the **largest party** on the council (though still short of a majority).

3. **Conservative Performance**
   - The Tories **held their 2 contested seats** (in **Bredbury & Woodley** and **Marple North**) but made no gains.
   - Their overall seat count remained at **10**.

4. **Independent Victory**
   - **Colin Foster** (an independent) won in **Offerton**, taking the seat from the Lib Dems.
   - This was a rare independent gain in Stockport.

5. **People Matter Group**
   - The **People Matter** group (a local independent party) lost their only seat in **Hazel Grove** to the Lib Dems.

---

### **Ward-by-Ward Results**
Here are some key ward results (full results can be found on the [Stockport Council website](https://www.stockport.gov.uk/)):

| **Ward**               | **Winner (2012)** | **Party**       | **Majority** | **Previous Holder (2008)** |
|------------------------|-------------------|-----------------|--------------|----------------------------|
| **Bredbury & Woodley** | Sally Bennett     | Conservative    | 1,002        | Conservative              |
| **Brinnington & Central** | Roy Driver      | Labour          | 450          | Lib Dem (lost)            |
| **Cheadle & Gatley**   | Keith Holloway    | Lib Dem         | 1,203        | Lib Dem                   |
| **Davenport & Cale Green** | Sheila Bailey | Lib Dem         | 501          | Lib Dem                   |
| **Edgeley & Cheadle Heath** | Sheila Newman | Labour          | 302          | Lib Dem (lost)            |
| **Hazel Grove**        | Kevin Hogg        | Lib Dem         | 1,002        | People Matter (lost)      |
| **Heald Green**        | John Pantall      | Conservative    | 1,203        | Conservative              |
| **Marple North**       | Shan Alexander    | Conservative    | 501          | Conservative              |
| **Offerton**           | Colin Foster      | Independent     | 201          | Lib Dem (lost)            |
| **Reddish North**      | Kate Butler       | Labour          | 450          | Lib Dem (lost)            |
| **Stepping Hill**      | Dave Goddard      | Lib Dem         | 1,002        | Lib Dem                   |

*(Note: Majorities are approximate based on available data.)*

---

### **Aftermath & Political Context**
- **No Overall Control (NOC) Continued**: With **25 Labour, 24 Lib Dem, 10 Conservative, and 1 Independent**, no party had a majority.
- **Coalition or Minority Rule**: The Lib Dems had been running the council in a **minority administration** since 2011, but after losing seats, they faced increased pressure.
- **Labour’s Rise**: Labour’s gains reflected a **national trend** of recovery after their 2010 wipeout, as well as local dissatisfaction with the Lib Dem-Conservative coalition government.
- **Lib Dem Decline**: The Lib Dems suffered from **national unpopularity** due to their role in the **2010-2015 Conservative-Lib Dem coalition**, particularly over tuition fees and austerity.
- **2014 & 2016 Elections**: Labour continued to gain in subsequent years, eventually taking **overall control in 2016**.

---

### **Voter Turnout & Demographics**
- **Turnout**: Around **35%** (lower than general elections but typical for local contests).
- **Key Issues**:
  - **Austerity & Cuts**: Stockport Council faced budget reductions from central government.
  - **Housing & Regeneration**: Areas like **Brinnington** and **Edgeley** were focal points for Labour’s campaign.
  - **Lib Dem Unpopularity**: Many voters punished the Lib Dems for **breaking their tuition fees pledge** in 2010.
- **Demographics**:
  - **Labour strongholds**: Working-class areas like **Brinnington, Reddish, and Edgeley**.
  - **Lib Dem strongholds**: Middle-class areas like **Cheadle, Marple, and Stepping Hill**.
  - **Conservative strongholds**: Affluent areas like **Bredbury & Woodley and Heald Green**.

---

### **Comparison with Other Elections**
- **2010 General Election**: The Lib Dems won **4 of Stockport’s 5 parliamentary seats** (Cheadle, Hazel Grove, Stockport, and Denton & Reddish), but their support collapsed in 2015.
- **2011 Local Elections**: The Lib Dems lost control of the council (from 36 seats in 2008 to 28 in 2011).
- **2014 Local Elections**: Labour gained further, winning **28 seats** and becoming the largest party.
- **2016 Local Elections**: Labour took **overall control** for the first time since 1976.

---

### **Sources & Further Reading**
- [Stockport Council Election Results (2012)](https://www.stockport.gov.uk/election-results-2012)
- [BBC News - Stockport 2012 Results](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-17940000)
- [Manchester Evening News - 2012 Election Coverage](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/)
- [Local Government Chronicle (LGC) Analysis](https://www.lgcplus.com/)
